chunks: 3594 - Sharif ibn Sabiq al-Taflisi narrated from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrah al-Samandi al-Kufi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:
“Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud عليه السلام: ‘You are an excellent servant, were it not that you eat from the public treasury and do not do any work with your hand.’”
He said: “Then Dawud عليه السلام wept, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the iron:”

“So it became soft, and Allah, Exalted is He, made the iron pliable for him. He used to make one coat of armor each day and sell it for one thousand dirhams. He عليه السلام made three hundred and sixty coats of armor and sold them for three hundred and sixty thousand dirhams, and thus became independent of the public treasury.”

key_terms.أَوْحَى: revealed or inspired by divine communication
key_terms.اسْتَغْنَى: became independent and no longer in need
key_terms.الْحَدِيدِ: iron, which Allah made pliable for Dawud عليه السلام
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury from which communal funds are distributed
key_terms.دَاوُدَ: Prophet Dawud عليه السلام, to whom this divine instruction was given
key_terms.دِرْعًا: a coat of armor crafted and sold as a means of livelihood
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a silver coin used here to indicate the sale price

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Prophet Dawud عليه السلام earning his livelihood by working with his own hands?
ai.summary: This narration presents Dawud عليه السلام as a model of honorable livelihood through personal labor rather than dependence on public funds. It highlights the virtue of working with one’s own hands, while also connecting this account to the Qur'anic sign of iron being softened for Dawud عليه السلام.
